headline: Westfield rejects permit extension for long-delayed data-center campus
dek: The unanimous vote ends the current approval for Servistar Realties’ more than 150-acre project, though the developer can appeal within 20 days.
body: Westfield’s Planning Board has rejected a permit extension for a proposed hyperscale data-center campus, closing the current approval after five years of delay and leaving the developer with 20 days to appeal. The board voted unanimously Tuesday, Oct. 13, that Servistar Realties had not shown good cause to extend its special permit, according to New England Public Media reporting carried by [WBUR](https://www.wbur.org/news/2026/10/14/westfield-data-center-plan).

The decision concerns a project planned for more than 150 acres near Route 202 and Servistar Industrial Way. The [city’s official agenda](https://www.cityofwestfield.org/AgendaCenter/PreviousVersions/_10132026-8701) identified Servistar’s request as unfinished business for the Oct. 13 special meeting and described it as a permit extension for a data center off Ampad Road and Servistar Industrial Way. [WAMC](https://www.wamc.org/news/2026-10-13/long-awaited-westfield-data-center-permit-extension-vote-on-tuesday-agenda?_amp=true) reported that the developer had sought a three-year extension after the board postponed a decision in September.

The permit had been approved in 2021, while the developer has been working on the proposal since 2019. During that time, Servistar began discussions with Westfield Gas & Electric about energy supply and hired environmental surveyors to delineate wetlands on the proposed property. But the company had not purchased the land planned for the campus, a point that became central to the board’s review, according to WBUR’s account of the meeting.

Paul Corey, a Servistar representative, told the board that the project’s delays were tied to the timing of state tax incentives, financing conditions and broader market disruptions. He cited tariffs, supply-chain problems, chip costs and natural-gas prices as factors that complicated the project. Board members did not find those explanations persuasive enough to justify another extension, and they also questioned the developer’s communication and project preparation.

Board members raised procedural concerns as well. WBUR reported that Servistar Realties’ limited-liability-company status had lapsed in late 2024 and that the original special permit had not been registered with the Hampden County Registry of Deeds. Those details do not establish that the data-center proposal violated every applicable requirement, but they helped explain why the board concluded that the developer had not demonstrated good cause for more time.

The vote does not erase the possibility of further legal or administrative action. Under state law, Servistar may appeal the board’s decision within 20 days, according to WBUR. Until an appeal or another approved path changes the situation, however, the existing permit will expire at the end of October and the project has no current authorization to advance under that approval.

Westfield’s decision also fits into a broader regional debate over large computing facilities. The city council adopted a one-year moratorium on new data centers in July, but the Servistar proposal was exempt because it was already in progress. WAMC reported before the vote that critics had raised concerns about communication, possible pressure on the electric grid and the project’s effect on the community. Those concerns are part of the policy debate; they are not a finding that the rejected project caused a specific grid or environmental harm.

For Westfield, the immediate result is a pause in the most advanced data-center proposal in the city while the appeal period runs. The board’s action leaves several practical questions open, including whether Servistar will challenge the decision, what will happen to the undeveloped property and whether another developer could pursue a different use. The city’s moratorium and the failed extension mean any future data-center proposal would face a different local policy landscape than the one Servistar entered in 2021.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Westfield rejects Servistar data-center permit extension
seoDescription: Westfield’s Planning Board unanimously denied a permit extension for Servistar Realties’ long-delayed hyperscale data-center campus.
